verdict: Danaher's revenue rose 8.5% to $6.6B as the Masimo acquisition lifted Diagnostics, and a $263M one-off tax benefit pushed net earnings up 36% to $1.2B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $1.27 a year ago — $1.71 from continuing operations plus $0.04 from discontinued operations; adjusted EPS was $2.11

kpis.label: Diagnostics revenue
kpis.note: +17% YoY, lifted by the Masimo acquisition; underlying core growth was 0.5%

kpis.label: Operating cash flow
kpis.note: Free cash flow was $1.6B on Danaher's non-GAAP measure

segments.name: Biotechnology
segments.note: Tools and consumables that help drugmakers research, develop and manufacture biotech medicines. Up 1% YoY in reported sales; core sales (excluding deals and currency) rose 5%.

segments.name: Life Sciences
segments.note: Instruments, reagents and consumables for laboratory research. Up 4% YoY; core sales rose 4.5%.

segments.name: Diagnostics
segments.note: Clinical lab instruments, tests and patient monitoring — now the biggest segment at 44% of sales. Up 17% YoY, almost all of it from buying Masimo, a patient-monitoring company; core sales rose just 0.5% as respiratory-test sales fell.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company, including $513M of amortization — writing down the value of technology and brands bought in acquisitions, a bookkeeping charge rather than cash.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new instruments, tests and monitoring products. Up 15% YoY.

otherDetail: Other expense was $85M, net: $135M of interest expense and $9M of other expense, partly offset by $31M of interest income — net non-operating expense of $113M on Danaher's own statement — partly offset in turn by $28M of earnings from discontinued operations, a tax benefit from releasing old tax reserves tied to businesses Danaher has since separated (see one-offs). Folding that $28M in here is what lets the flow tie to total net earnings of $1,235M; profit from continuing operations alone was $1,207M.
follow100Note: The rows reconcile to the profit row within a cent or two of rounding.

takeaways.title: Growth came mostly from a deal
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 8.5% to $6.6B. Diagnostics jumped 17% to $2.9B, almost entirely because Danaher bought Masimo, a patient-monitoring company that had about $1.5B of sales in 2025. Stripping out deals and currency, core revenue rose 3.0%, or 5.5% excluding respiratory-testing products, whose sales are fading.

takeaways.title: A tax one-off flattered the bottom line
takeaways.text: Net earnings rose 36% to $1.2B, but much of the jump was tax: Danaher booked a $263M discrete tax benefit — releasing reserves set aside for uncertain tax positions after audits were settled — which turned its tax line into a $75M benefit instead of a charge, a -6.6% effective tax rate. Profit from continuing operations was $1,207M.

takeaways.title: Core profitability held steady
takeaways.text: Operating profit rose 8% to $1.2B, a 19.0% operating margin — about the same as a year ago. Operating cash flow was a strong $1.9B. Just after quarter end Danaher also closed its $1.4B purchase of StatLab, a lab-consumables maker, which joins Diagnostics in the fourth quarter.

oneTimers: Discrete tax benefit of $263M: Danaher released reserves for uncertain tax positions after audit settlements, cutting its effective tax rate by 23.2 percentage points and turning the quarter's tax line into a $75M net benefit. This is a one-off — it is the main reason reported profit grew so much faster than operating profit.

Earnings from discontinued operations of $28M were also a tax benefit: releasing reserves on old tax returns Danaher filed jointly with Veralto and Fortive before those businesses were separated from Danaher. It is folded into the other-expense line so the flow ties to total net earnings.

Costs include a $52M impairment charge in the Biotechnology segment — writing down the value of a facility — booked in cost of sales, and an $84M pre-tax charge in Diagnostics from writing up Masimo's inventory to fair value at acquisition and then selling it (a standard deal-accounting charge that fades as that inventory is sold).
footerNote: Danaher reports in whole $M; no rounding adjustment was needed. See otherDetail for how the $28M of discontinued-operations earnings is folded into the flow.
